subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and should that cache live only inside one reviewer/run keyed by the full reviewed input?
rationale: The defect is source-reproducible and the fix is small, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes approval review freshness for a security-sensitive execution path.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower behavior change with fewer savings.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated reviewer completion cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until maintainers want a broader approval-cache policy.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent auto-review area history make this the strongest available owner for the exec approval cache-boundary decision.
